title: Kernel of the coordinate restriction map
statement: Fix a prime $p$ and let $V = \bbf_p^n \times \bbf_p^n$. For a subset $E \subseteq \{1,\dots,n\}$, let $r_E \colon V \to V_E$ be the restriction map that keeps the coordinates indexed by $E$ and sets all others to zero. Then the kernel of $r_E$ is the support submodule $V_{E^c}$ consisting of those vectors whose support lies in the complement $E^c = \{1,\dots,n\} \setminus E$; that is, $r_E$ annihilates exactly the vectors that vanish on every coordinate in $E$.
hypotheses_covered: E is a subset of the coordinate index set Fin n
replaced: $\ker(r_E) = V_{\mathrm{univ} \setminus E}$, the subspace supported on the complement of $E$.
